mainTopic: When we mention rain in the עמידה, why it is called גבורות גשמים, why it belongs in תפילה, and the three keys God keeps for Himself
overview: The first משנה of מסכת תענית asks from when we start saying משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם in the עמידה. רבי אליעזר says from the first day of סוכות, and רבי יהושע says from the last day, שמיני עצרת. רבי אליעזר explains that mentioning rain is only praise, not a request. רבי יהושע answers that if so, it could be said all year. The משנה adds that we actually ask for rain only close to the rainy season, and רבי יהודה describes which חזן starts and stops the mention. The גמרא asks what earlier source the משנה builds on and points first to ברכות, then explains that the משנה follows ראש השנה's teaching that the world is judged for water on סוכות. It explains the term גבורות גשמים through a גזירה שוה linking rain to the creation of the world, and it learns from 'service of the heart' that rain belongs in תפילה. Finally, רבי יוחנן teaches that God keeps three keys for Himself, rain, childbirth, and תחיית המתים, and the proof for childbirth continues on the next amud.

steps.title: From when do we mention rain? Two opinions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks when we begin mentioning the power of rain in davening. רבי אליעזר says from the first day of סוכות, and רבי יהושע says from the last day.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when do we mention the might of the rains? רבי אליעזר says: from the first יום טוב of the חג (סוכות). רבי יהושע says: from the last יום טוב of the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a question about the start date for saying משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם. Two תנאים give two different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Mentioning the might of rain' means praising ה׳'s power to bring rain inside the second ברכה of the עמידה, the ברכה of תחיית המתים. רבי אליעזר starts on the first day of סוכות, and רבי יהושע waits until the last יום טוב, which is שמיני עצרת. The rest of the משנה explains the reasoning behind each side.

keyTerms.meaning: The might of rain, meaning ה׳'s power to bring rain
The first festival day of סוכות
The last festival day of סוכות, which is שמיני עצרת

phrases.english: From when do we mention the might of the rains?
phrases.notes: Refers to saying 'He makes the wind blow and the rain fall' in the עמידה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִיּוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: from the first festival day of the Festival (Sukkot).
phrases.notes: In the משנה, 'חג' with no other name means סוכות.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מִיּוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: from the last festival day of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the מסכת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute: רבי אליעזר begins mentioning rain on the first day of סוכות, and רבי יהושע begins on שמיני עצרת.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: rain on סוכות is a bad sign
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע challenges רבי אליעזר. Since rain during סוכות is a sign of a curse, why mention it then?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: Since rain on the חג is nothing but a sign of a curse, why should one mention it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע attacks רבי אליעזר's opinion. He argues that it makes no sense to bring up rain during סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain on סוכות forces people out of the סוכה, so it is a סימן קללה. רבי יהושע assumes that mentioning rain is like asking for it. In that case, mentioning it on סוכות would mean asking for something bad.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים אֶלָּא סִימַן קְלָלָה בֶּחָג,
phrases.english: Since rain is nothing but a sign of a curse on the Festival,
phrases.notes: Rain drives people out of their סוכות.

phrases.english: why should he mention it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הוֹאִיל וְאֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים אֶלָּא סִימַן קְלָלָה בֶּחָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's opinion from step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling to start mentioning rain on the first day of סוכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rain on סוכות is a curse, so mentioning it, which is assumed to be a request, would be asking for a curse.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: mentioning is not asking
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that he never said to ask for rain on סוכות. He only said to mention, as praise, that ה׳ brings rain in its season.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: I too did not say to request rain. I said only to mention 'He makes the wind blow and the rain fall' in its season.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends himself. He separates 'mentioning' rain from 'asking' for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם is praise of ה׳'s power, not a prayer for rain to fall now. Praising ה׳ for rain that comes 'in its season' does not invite rain during סוכות. So רבי יהושע's challenge does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: He makes the wind blow and the rain fall

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up הזכרה and שאלה. הזכרה is 'משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם' in the second ברכה, and it is praise. שאלה is 'ותן טל ומטר' in ברכת השנים, and it is an actual request. Much of this מסכת depends on keeping these two apart.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between praising (הזכרה) and requesting (שאלה) explains why our סידור has two separate insertions for rain, each with its own start date.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
I too did not say to request
phrases.notes: He agrees that one should not ask for rain on סוכות.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְהַזְכִּיר ״מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ וּמוֹרִיד הַגֶּשֶׁם״ בְּעוֹנָתוֹ.
phrases.english: but only to mention 'He makes the wind blow and the rain fall' in its season.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי לִשְׁאוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the action: mentioning is praise, not a request
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning rain is the same as asking for it, so it would be asking for a curse on סוכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Mentioning is only praise of ה׳'s power to bring rain in its season, so it is fine on סוכות.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: then mention it all year
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע pushes back. If mentioning is only praise and not a request, it could be said all year round.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, one should always mention it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע turns רבי אליעזר's answer against him. If mentioning rain is not a request, nothing should stop us from saying it every day of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once mentioning is just praise, it no longer seems tied to any season. So why start on סוכות at all? רבי יהושע's point is that the mention must have some link to the actual rainy season, which supports starting at the end of the חג, when rain is wanted.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
one should always mention it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ אִם כֵּן לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אליעזר's answer in step 3 with a new challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's claim that mentioning is only praise
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If mentioning is not a request, it has no reason to be limited to any season, so it should be said all year.

steps.title: We request rain only close to the rainy season
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states a general rule. We actually ask for rain only near the time when rain is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not request rain except close to the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a rule about שאלה, the actual request for rain. It must be made only near the rainy season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that asking for rain, unlike mentioning it, belongs only close to the time of rain. This sets the request apart from the mention and shows that it has its own timing.

phrases.english: We do not request rain
except close to the rainy season.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין שׁוֹאֲלִים אֶת הַגְּשָׁמִים אֶלָּא סָמוּךְ לַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate about mentioning to a rule about requesting
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An actual request for rain (שאלה) is made only near the rainy season.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: which prayer leader starts and stops
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains the switch-over. On שמיני עצרת, the מוסף חזן mentions rain and the שחרית חזן does not. On the first day of פסח, the שחרית חזן mentions rain and the מוסף חזן does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the one who goes before the ark on the last יום טוב of the חג: the last one mentions, and the first one does not. On the first יום טוב of פסח: the first one mentions, and the last one does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the exact point within the day when the mention of rain begins and ends. He does this by naming which חזן says it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The first' is the חזן for שחרית, and 'the last' is the חזן for מוסף. So the mention begins at מוסף of שמיני עצרת and ends after שחרית of the first day of פסח. This matches our practice today, where the change happens at מוסף on both days.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who goes before the ark, meaning the חזן
The last one, the מוסף leader
The first one, the שחרית leader
Passover, when the mention of rain stops

steps.whatToRemember: The rainy season's mention runs from מוסף of שמיני עצרת until מוסף of the first day of פסח. The מוסף חזן starts it in the fall and stops it in the spring.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The one who passes before the ark
on the last festival day of the Festival:
the last one (Musaf) mentions; the first one (Shacharit) does not mention.
On the first festival day of Passover:
the first one mentions; the last one does not mention.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר הָעוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds precise timing within the day for starting and stopping the mention
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mention begins at מוסף of שמיני עצרת and ends at מוסף of the first day of פסח.

steps.title: גמרא asks: what is the משנה building on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the תנא is coming from when he opens with 'from when.' The question assumes we already know there is an obligation to mention rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Where is the תנא standing, that he teaches 'from when'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking about the משנה's first word. 'From when' assumes the obligation to mention rain was already taught somewhere, so where was that?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A question about 'when' only makes sense if you already know that we mention rain at all. Our משנה never says this, so it must rely on an earlier source. The גמרא wants to find that source.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
Where is he standing? (What is he based on?)

phrases.english: Gemara: Where is the tanna standing,
that he teaches 'from when'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins analyzing the opening word of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What earlier source establishes the obligation to mention rain, which the משנה's 'from when' takes for granted?

steps.title: The תנא is standing 'there'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא is relying on a source 'there,' meaning another משנה. The source itself is spelled out next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא is standing there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by saying the תנא is based on a משנה somewhere else. This line sets up the next move, where the גמרא will quote that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'There' refers to the משנה in מסכת ברכות, which teaches that we mention גבורות גשמים in the ברכה of תחיית המתים. Because that משנה already established the obligation, our משנה can simply ask when it starts. The full quote continues next.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in another place (מסכת ברכות)

phrases.english: The tanna is standing there:
phrases.notes: The answer continues into the next passage with the quote from ברכות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה builds on an earlier משנה (in מסכת ברכות) that already established the obligation to mention rain. The details continue next.

steps.title: The source in ברכות that sets up the obligation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in ברכות: we mention rain in תחיית המתים, we ask for rain in ברכת השנים, and הבדלה goes in חונן הדעת. Building on that, our משנה asks 'from when.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As the משנה in ברכות teaches: we mention the might of rain in the blessing of תחיית המתים, we ask for rain in ברכת השנים, and we say הבדלה in חונן הדעת. Then our משנה teaches: from when do we mention the might of rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the 'source over there' it mentioned in step 8. It is a משנה in ברכות that already teaches we must mention rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 7 was how the תנא can ask 'from when' before telling us there is any obligation at all. The answer is that the obligation is already known from ברכות. Our משנה only adds the timing.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'might of rain': mentioning rain as praise in the שמונה עשרה
The second ברכה of שמונה עשרה (מחיה מתים)
The ninth ברכה (ברך עלינו), where we ask for rain
The fourth ברכה, where אתה חוננתנו (הבדלה) is added

steps.confusionAlert: Keep these two separate. Mentioning rain (הזכרה, in תחיית המתים) is praise. Asking for rain (שאלה, in ברכת השנים) is a request. They happen in different ברכות.

phrases.english: As it teaches: One mentions the might of the rains
in the blessing of the resurrection of the dead,
and one requests rain in the blessing of the years,
and havdalah is said in 'Who graciously grants knowledge.'
phrases.notes: This line is part of the quote from ברכות 33a.

phrases.english: And [based on that] it teaches: From when does one mention the might of the rains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 8 by naming the source it pointed to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The obligation to mention rain comes from the משנה in ברכות. Our משנה only adds when it starts.

steps.title: Then why not teach the timing in ברכות?
steps.stepSummary: If the timing builds on ברכות, the תנא should have taught it there. Why wait until מסכת תענית?
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him teach it there! What is different that he left it until here?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. If our משנה is really a follow-up to ברכות, it belongs in ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A follow-up rule should sit next to the rule it builds on. ברכות is at the start of סדר זרעים, and תענית is far away in סדר מועד, so the placement makes no sense under the first answer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let him teach it there': why not put it in the other place?

phrases.english: So let him teach it there!
What is different that he left it until here?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in steps 8 and 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that our משנה continues the משנה in ברכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A continuation should be taught in the same place, not many מסכתות later.

steps.title: The תנא is coming from ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The real link is מסכת ראש השנה, which teaches that on סוכות the world is judged for water. That naturally leads to 'from when do we mention rain.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the תנא is coming from ראש השנה, as we learned there: 'On the חג (סוכות) the world is judged for water.' Since he taught that, he went on to teach: from when do we mention the might of rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the ברכות link as the reason for the placement. It explains that תענית picks up right where ראש השנה left off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא means the earlier answer is being replaced as the explanation for where the משנה sits. מסכת ראש השנה, which comes right before תענית, taught that on סוכות the world is judged for water. That leads naturally into the question of when, around סוכות, we start mentioning rain. The obligation itself is still known from ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Is coming up from / just finished
On סוכות the world is judged for water
Since he [already] taught: one topic leads into the next

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows מסכת ראש השנה. The judgment for water on סוכות leads into the question of when we start mentioning rain.

phrases.english: Rather, the tanna is coming from [tractate] Rosh HaShana,
as we learned: And on the festival they are judged for water.
And since he taught
'And on the festival they are judged for water,'
he taught: From when does one mention the might of the rains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the explanation for where the משנה is placed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה was placed here because it continues ברכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was placed here because it follows ראש השנה's teaching about the judgment for water on סוכות.

steps.title: Why the wording 'might of rain'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה says גבורות גשמים instead of simply 'mentioning rain.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him just teach 'from when do we mention rain.' Why say 'the might of rain'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic: the exact wording of the משנה. It asks why the extra word גבורות is there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain wording would have been enough to teach the rule. So the extra word must be telling us something about rain itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Mentioning rain (the simpler wording the גמרא suggests)

phrases.english: Let him teach: 'From when does one mention the rains.'
What is 'the might of the rains'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the משנה's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה adds the word גבורות

steps.title: Rain falls with divine power
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that rain comes down with גבורה. He proves it from two פסוקים in איוב that put rain right after God's great wonders.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Because rain falls with might. As it says, 'He does great things beyond understanding, wonders without number,' and it is written, 'Who gives rain on the earth and sends water on the fields.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the wording question. Rain is called 'mighty' because it shows God's power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק speaks of God's endless great wonders. The very next פסוק names rain. This shows that rain is one of those great acts of power, which is why the משנה calls it גבורות.
steps.whatToRemember: גבורות גשמים means rain is a display of God's power. That is why we mention it in the ברכה of מחיה מתים, which praises God's גבורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because they fall with might,
as it is stated: 'Who does great things beyond comprehension,'
'and wonders without number,'
and it is written: 'Who gives rain upon the earth,'
'and sends water upon the fields.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיּוֹרְדִין בִּגְבוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rain is called גבורות because it falls with divine might, as shown by the פסוקים in איוב.

steps.title: How do those verses show that rain is a mighty act?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the פסוקים רבי יוחנן quoted actually show that rain comes with גבורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is that implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks how the verses from איוב prove that rain involves גבורה, since neither verse uses that word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's verses call God's acts 'great' and place rain right after them. They never say גבורה. So the גמרא wants to see the actual link to 'might.'

keyTerms.meaning: What implies it? / How is this shown?

phrases.english: From where is it implied?
phrases.notes: It asks how the verses from איוב show that rain is a 'mighty' act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי יוחנן's verses really prove his point.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the verses in איוב prove that rain is connected to גבורה.

steps.title: A word-link to the creation of the world
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא answers with a גזירה שוה: the word חקר appears both in the rain verse and in a verse about creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said: We learn it from the word 'חקר' (beyond understanding) here and the word 'חקר' in the passage about the creation of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שילא answers the question. The word חקר shows up in two places, so we connect them, and rain becomes like the creation of the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה uses a shared word to carry an idea from one פסוק to another. Here the shared word links rain to creation. The next step will show where creation is described with גבורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the answer
It comes / it is learned (signals a גזירה שוה)
Searching out / understanding; 'beyond חקר' means beyond understanding

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the word גבורה in the rain verse. The proof works in two links: rain is tied to creation by the shared word חקר, and creation is tied to גבורה by a separate פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Sheila said:
It is learned from 'comprehension' and 'comprehension'
phrases.notes: A גזירה שוה based on the shared word.

phrases.english: from the creation of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word חקר links rain to the creation of the world.

steps.title: Spelling out the verses: rain, creation, and might
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא quotes three verses. The rain verse in איוב uses חקר, the creation verse in ישעיהו uses חקר, and a verse in תהלים describes creation with גבורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here (about rain) it is written: 'He does great things beyond understanding.' There (about creation) it is written: 'Have you not known? Have you not heard? The everlasting God, ה׳, Creator of the ends of the earth, does not grow tired or weary; His understanding is beyond searching.' And it is written (about creation): 'He sets up the mountains with His strength; He is girded with might.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא spells out the proof. Both rain and creation are 'beyond חקר.' Creation is described with the word גבורה. So rain is a גבורה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain runs like this: rain equals creation (shared word חקר), and creation equals גבורה (the פסוק in תהלים). That is why the משנה calls it גבורות גשמים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here… and it is written there (the standard form for laying out a גזירה שוה)
Creator of the ends of the earth

steps.whatToRemember: Rain counts as גבורה because it is linked to the creation of the world, and creation was done with גבורה.

phrases.english: It is written here:
phrases.notes: Here, in איוב, right before the mention of rain.

phrases.english: 'Who does great things beyond comprehension,'
and it is written there:
'Have you not known? Have you not heard

phrases.aramaic: אֱלֹהֵי עוֹלָם ה׳ בּוֹרֵא קְצוֹת הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: the everlasting God, the Lord, Creator of the ends of the earth
does not grow faint and does not grow weary
His discernment is beyond comprehension,'
and it is written: 'Who sets firm the mountains with His strength,
girded with might.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the verses behind the גזירה שוה of step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That rain is an act of גבורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 5:9, ישעיהו 40:28, and תהלים 65:7, linked by the word חקר.

steps.title: Where do we learn that rain belongs in prayer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that rain should be mentioned specifically in תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that rain is mentioned in prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question. We know rain is a גבורה, but why does it belong in תפילה (the עמידה)?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling rain 'mighty' explains its name. It does not yet explain why it has a place in our prayers. The גמרא now looks for that source.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is in prayer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why rain is called גבורה to why it appears in תפילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for mentioning rain in תפילה.

steps.title: Service of the heart is prayer, and rain comes right after
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'serving God with your heart' means תפילה. The next פסוק promises rain, so rain belongs in תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'To love ה׳ your God and to serve Him with all your heart.' What kind of service is done in the heart? You must say: this is prayer. And right after it is written: 'I will give the rain of your land in its time, the early rain and the late rain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Prayer is 'service of the heart,' and the פסוק about rain comes right after it, so the two go together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים in קריאת שמע (the second paragraph) sit next to each other: one about serving with the heart, one about rain. Because they are placed side by side, the ברייתא learns that rain should be mentioned during prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: Service in the heart, which means prayer
You must say / it must be
The early (autumn) rain and the late (spring) rain

steps.whatToRemember: תפילה is called עבודה שבלב, and because the promise of rain comes right after it in the Torah, we mention rain in תפילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for calling תפילה 'service of the heart,' an idea that shows up throughout הלכות תפילה.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
'To love the Lord your God
and to serve Him with all your heart,'
which is the service that is in the heart?
You must say: this is prayer.
And it is written right after it:
'And I will give the rain of your land in its due time,
the first rain and the last rain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Prayer is עבודה שבלב, and the פסוק about rain directly follows it, so rain is mentioned in prayer.

steps.title: Three keys God keeps for Himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that God personally holds three keys, never handed to a messenger: rain, childbirth, and תחיית המתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Three keys are in the hand of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and were never given to a messenger. They are: the key of rain, the key of childbirth, and the key of the resurrection of the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new related teaching. רבי יוחנן says three things are controlled by God directly, with no angel or messenger in between.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds to the idea that rain shows God's own power. Rain is listed together with תחיית המתים, which fits well with mentioning rain in the ברכה of תחיית המתים. The גמרא will next bring sources for each key.
steps.confusionAlert: Here חַיָּה does not mean 'animal.' In this context it means a woman giving birth.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why rain sits next to תחיית המתים in the same ברכה: both are things God does Himself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Three keys are in the hand
of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
which were not handed over to a messenger,
and they are: the key of rain,
the key of childbirth,
and the key of the resurrection of the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new related statement showing that rain is God's direct power.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain, childbirth, and תחיית המתים are controlled by God directly, not through any messenger.

steps.title: The proof that God holds the key of rain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק from דברים showing that God Himself 'opens' the heavens to give rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The key of rain: as it says, "God will open for you His good treasure, the heavens, to give the rain of your land in its proper time."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now proves the first of רבי יוחנן's three keys. It shows from a פסוק that God Himself opens the storehouse of rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said God keeps the key of rain in His own hands. The פסוק says 'ה׳ will open' (יִפְתַּח), so God Himself is the one opening, not a שליח. The word 'open' fits the image of a key opening a storehouse.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects back to the bigger theme of the סוגיא. Rain comes directly from God, which is why it belongs in תפילה and is linked to גבורה.

phrases.english: The key of rain — as it is written:
"The Lord will open for you His good treasure,
phrases.notes: דברים כח:יב. 'ה׳ will open' means God Himself, not a messenger.

phrases.aramaic: אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם לָתֵת מְטַר אַרְצְךָ בְּעִתּוֹ״.
phrases.english: the heavens, to give the rain of your land in its time."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural source for the first key (rain) in רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That the key of rain is held by God Himself and not given to a שליח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים כח:יב — יִפְתַּח ה׳ לְךָ אֶת אוֹצָרוֹ הַטּוֹב אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם לָתֵת מְטַר אַרְצְךָ בְּעִתּוֹ

steps.title: The proof that God holds the key of childbirth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the key of childbirth and begins quoting the פסוק about God remembering רחל.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know about the key of childbirth? As it says, "And God remembered רחל, and listened..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the second key, childbirth, and asks for its source. It starts quoting the פסוק about רחל, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רחל could not have children until God Himself 'remembered' her and 'opened her womb.' That shows God directly controls childbirth. The word 'opened' appears at the end of the פסוק, on the next amud, and matches the idea of a key.
steps.confusionAlert: Here חַיָּה does NOT mean 'animal.' It means a woman in childbirth, so 'the key of חיה' is the key of birth.

phrases.english: The key of childbirth — from where do we know it?
As it is written: "And God remembered Rachel
and listened...
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues on the next amud: 'to her, and opened her womb.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to Step 20; it moves from the first key (rain) to the second key (childbirth).
steps.raayaObject: That the key of childbirth is held by God Himself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית ל:כב — וַיִּזְכֹּר אֱלֹהִים אֶת רָחֵל וַיִּשְׁמַע (continued on the next amud: אֵלֶיהָ אֱלֹהִים וַיִּפְתַּח אֶת רַחְמָהּ)
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the key of childbirth.
